results.title: India's New Drone Hunter Fires 64 Missiles In 10 Seconds, Challenges Pakistan's Swarm Strategy
results.description: Drone warfare has changed the battlefield forever. From Ukraine to West Asia and Operation Sindoor, low-cost drone swarms have exposed the limitations of traditional air-defence systems. India is now preparing its own answer—Bhargavastra. The indigenous vehicle-mounted system combines radar, electro-optical sensors, passive RF detection and a launcher carrying 64 micro-missiles and rockets capable of engaging multiple drones in rapid succession. Unlike electronic jamming systems, Bhargavastra is a hard-kill solution designed to physically destroy incoming threats. With internal trials expected to conclude within months, the system is moving closer to user evaluation by the armed forces. This video explains the technology, the significance of the recent Army demonstration, the role Bhargavastra could play in Mission Sudarshan Chakra, and why India's defence strategy is rapidly shifting towards defeating autonomous warfare

results.title: Observatory downgrades typhoon signal to T3
results.description: The Observatory downgraded the T8 signal to the Strong Wind Signal No. 3 at 12.40 pm on Sunday. The forecaster cautioned that mean wind speeds of 41 to 62 kilometres per hour are expected. Authorities have urged the public to remain vigilant and stressed that it is not yet safe for small vessels to leave typhoon shelters. At noon, Severe Tropical Storm Noul was positioned about 110 kilometres north of Hong Kong, tracking north-northwest at roughly 15 kilometres per hour towards inland Guangdong. Acting Senior Scientific Officer Ng Yin-lam said that although gale-force south-westerly winds were still affecting parts of the territory, they would gradually subside as Noul moves away. "Under the influence of the intense outer rainbands associated with Noul, there will still be heavy squally showers and thunderstorms over the territory on Sunday," she said. Ng also advised residents to avoid water sports, as seas are expected to remain rough with high swells. Edited by Tony Sabine
